--- title: "Python" jupyter: coi-docs --- Everything below runs at build time against the live catalog — this page's own output is real, not copied. ## Install ```sh pip install duckdb ``` ## Attach and query ::: {#2d471990 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import duckdb con = duckdb.connect() con.execute("INSTALL iceberg; LOAD iceberg; INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;") con.execute( "ATTACH 'canceronice' AS coi (TYPE ICEBERG, " "ENDPOINT 'https://icegate-canceronice.seandavi.workers.dev', " "AUTHORIZATION_TYPE 'none');" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` <_duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection at 0x7feddba8a1b0> ``` ::: ::: Mammography screening in Colorado counties, lowest first, with the interval, the release that said so, and the county's rurality code: ::: {#ade262d3 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} con.sql(""" SELECT u.name, o.source_release, o.value AS pct, o.lower, o.upper, o.value_status, r.value AS rucc_code FROM coi.measure.observation o JOIN coi.geography.unit u ON u.geo_id = o.geo_id AND u.vintage = 2026 AND u.valid_to IS NULL LEFT JOIN coi.measure.observation r ON r.geo_id = o.geo_id AND r.source = 'RUCC' AND r.valid_to IS NULL WHERE o.source = 'PLACES' AND o.measure_id = 'PLACES:MAMMOUSE:age_adjusted' AND o.source_release = '2025' AND u.parent_geo_id = 'state:08' AND o.valid_to IS NULL ORDER BY pct LIMIT 10 """).df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: `u.vintage = 2026` is named explicitly rather than trusting `o.geo_vintage` — see [Concepts › Time axes](/concepts/time-axes.qmd) for why a measure's own `geo_vintage` column isn't always the vintage its `geo_id` actually belongs to (tracked as [#21](https://github.com/seandavi/cancer-on-ice/issues/21)). `con.sql(...)` returns a DuckDB relation; `.df()` materializes it as a pandas `DataFrame`, `.arrow()` as an Arrow table, or iterate it directly — whatever the rest of your analysis expects.
